newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM, Metsaliitto say domestic restructuring over.
newsitem.headline: UPM, Metsaliitto say domestic restructuring over.

text.p: Finnish forest industry groups UPM-Kymmene Oy and Metsaliitto said on Tuesday they saw scant scope for further major restructuring between Finnish forest firms.

UPM-Kymmene and Metsaliitto earlier on Tuesday announced a complicated series of deals. UPM-Kymmene units were sold to Metsaliitto's Metsa-Serla subsidiary and to their jointly-owned Metsa-Botnia pulp producer.
"It is impossible to say at this stage, but I think that major domestic arrangements would be extremely difficult," UPM-Kymmene CEO Juha Niemela told Reuters.
Competition authorities could stop major domestic mergers or acquisitions. Finland now has three big forest industry groups, the third being Enso Oy.
Asked whether overseas restructuring was in sight, Niemela said: "Overseas arrangements will take place in due course, if they happen." He declined to elaborate.

Metsaliitto CEO Antti Oksanen also said most of the restructuring in the Finnish forest industry had probably already been carried out and from now on, acquisitions and mergers were more likely take place overseas.
"Many things will probably take place there. We will see what our and other Finnish companies' role is out there," he said, but did not say what kind of deals he expected.
